newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean vessels intrude into Southern waters.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean vessels intrude into Southern waters.

text.p: A North Korean naval patrol vessel and nine fishing boats intruded into South Korean waters on Thursday, a defence ministry official said.
The craft were spotted at around 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT) on the southern side of a nautical demarcation line and were intercepted by South Korean naval vessels, the official said.
They turned back after a one-hour stand-off.
The official could not confirm a Yonhap Television News report that the Northern vessel fired three mortar rounds at the South Korean navy.
The demarcation line that bisects the Korean peninsula -- and extends into coastal waters -- is a legacy of the 1950-53 Korean War, which ended in a truce.
Exactly one week ago, a Northern naval ship intruded South, but South Korean authorities said at the time they believed it was a mistake. No shots were fired.
